questions.title: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K
questions.statementMd:
Given an integer array `arr` and an integer `k`, return the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of **exactly** `k` elements.

Recomputing the sum of every window from scratch is too slow for the hidden tests. Slide the window instead.

**Constraints**

- `1 <= k <= arr.length <= 100000`
- `-1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000`

python.driver:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys, json
    _args = [json.loads(_l) for _l in sys.stdin.read().split("\n") if _l.strip() != ""]
    _out = Solution().maxSumSubarray(*_args)
    print(json.dumps(_out, separators=(",", ":")))

tests.explanation: The window [5,1,3] has the largest sum, 9.
Every window is negative. The best is [-1,-2] with sum -3.

questions.title: Longest Subarray with Sum K
questions.statementMd:
Given an integer array `arr` and an integer `k`, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum equals `k`. Return `0` if there is none.

The array can contain negative numbers and zeroes, so a plain two-pointer window is not enough.

**Constraints**

- `1 <= arr.length <= 100000`
- `-1000 <= arr[i] <= 1000`
- `-10000000 <= k <= 10000000`

python.driver:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys, json
    _args = [json.loads(_l) for _l in sys.stdin.read().split("\n") if _l.strip() != ""]
    _out = Solution().longestSubarrayWithSumK(*_args)
    print(json.dumps(_out, separators=(",", ":")))

tests.explanation: The whole array sums to 15, so the answer is its length, 6.
